review_notes: I read the whole file and the two private raw-series theorems line by line. I compared the bounded integer-part wrappers against each other and against `restrictToAddSubgroup`. I did not look up Mathlib API for the proposed lemmas. I couldn't compile anything, so the proposed lemma statements and sketches are untested. One uncertainty is the exact Subtype coercion shape for `Subring`-membership. Another is whether `HahnSeries.filter` needs `Classical` instances at the call sites. I did not report the repeated `hone`/`hg0` snippets or the `hqC` and `hrsupp` filter-support unfoldings as separate findings. They are short routine unfoldings.

findings.problem: The two private theorems contain the same non-trivial argument. The only differences are names (`b`/`c'`, `hb0`/`hc0`) and where `q`, `hq`, `hq0` come from. Each proof (1) shows `q⁻¹` is supported in `C` via `support_subset_of_mul_eq` applied to `q * q⁻¹ = 1`, (2) shows that every exponent of `q⁻¹ * filter (∉ C) c` is `≤ 0` and `∉ C` using `add_nonpos_of_mem_of_nonpos_of_not_mem` and `C.sub_mem`, and (3) derives that the coefficient at 0 vanishes. The blocks `hone`, `hinv`, `hprod` and `hzero` (lines 82–105 versus 136–153) are copied almost verbatim. A fix to the convexity reasoning has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private lemma before both theorems:
`private theorem support_inv_mul_discarded {C : AddSubgroup G} (hC : (C : Set G).OrdConnected) {q c : K⟦G⟧} (hq : q.support ⊆ (C : Set G)) (hq0 : q ≠ 0) (hc : c.support ⊆ Set.Iic 0) : (∀ g ∈ (q⁻¹ * HahnSeries.filter (fun g ↦ g ∉ C) c).support, g ≤ 0 ∧ g ∉ C) ∧ (q⁻¹ * HahnSeries.filter (fun g ↦ g ∉ C) c).coeff 0 = 0`.
Proof sketch: prove `hone` and `hinv` as in lines 82–89. Take `g` in the support and use `support_mul_subset` to get `a + b` with `a` in `supp q⁻¹ ⊆ C` and `b` in `supp (filter (∉ C) c)`. Then `b ≤ 0` and `b ∉ C`. The first conjunct follows from `add_nonpos_of_mem_of_nonpos_of_not_mem`, and the second from `C.sub_mem`. The coefficient claim is `by_contra` plus `hprod 0 ... |>.2 C.zero_mem`.
In `exists_integral_cofactor`, call it with `hq hq0 hc` and then `obtain ⟨hprod, hzero⟩`. In `exists_complementary_factor`, call it with `q := filter (· ∈ C) b`, `hq := hqC`, `hq0 := hne`, `hc := hb`. Both calls fit the actual hypotheses. The remaining `refine` blocks stay unchanged and use `hprod`/`hzero` exactly as before. The `hrsupp` step in each theorem becomes internal to the lemma.
findings.benefit: The convexity/inverse-support argument is the mathematical core of both results. It would be stated and proved once, and the two theorems would shrink by about 25 lines each to bookkeeping. A reader can then see that both results use the same estimate on `q⁻¹ * (discarded part)`.

findings.problem: Both bounded-integer-part theorems repeat the same transfer from a raw Hahn-series identity to a statement in `cardSuppLTTruncationIntegerPart`. They build the quotient in `CardSuppLTField` as `x / q`, show its raw series equals the cofactor via `mul_comm, mul_div_assoc, div_self, mul_one`, repackage it using `mem_cardSuppLTTruncationIntegerPart`, and close with `Subtype.ext` and `div_mul_cancel₀`. This is lines 249–272 versus 340–361. Separately, lines 301–308 rebuild the restriction `tf`/`t` by hand, with the same `cardSupp_mono (support_filter_subset ..)` membership proof and coefficient-0 filter step. That is exactly the definition `restrictToAddSubgroup` (lines 217–231), which is already available and has the `rfl` simp lemma `coe_restrictToAddSubgroup`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma in the `CardSuppLTTruncationIntegerPart` namespace:
`theorem exists_of_raw_mul_eq (Z : Subring K) (q x : cardSuppLTTruncationIntegerPart (G := G) (R := K) (κ := κ) Z) (hq0 : q ≠ 0) (v : K⟦G⟧) (hv : v.support ⊆ Set.Iic 0) (hv0 : v.coeff 0 ∈ Z) (hxv : (x : K⟦G⟧) = q * v) : ∃ w : cardSuppLTTruncationIntegerPart (G := G) (R := K) (κ := κ) Z, (w : K⟦G⟧) = v ∧ x = q * w`.
Proof sketch: this is lines 249–272 abstracted over `v`. Set `wf := (x : CardSuppLTField) / q`, prove its raw series is `v`, build the subtype element using `hv`/`hv0`, and prove `x = q * w` by `Subtype.ext` and `div_mul_cancel₀`.
Then `dvd_of_restriction_factorization` becomes `obtain ⟨v, hv, hv0, hxv⟩ := exists_integral_cofactor ..; obtain ⟨w', -, hw'⟩ := exists_of_raw_mul_eq Z q x hq0 v hv hv0 hxv; exact ⟨w', hw'⟩`.
`exists_factorization_by_restriction` takes `t := restrictToAddSubgroup Z C b`, whose raw series is `filter (· ∈ C) b` by `coe_restrictToAddSubgroup` / `rfl`. It gets `t ≠ 0` from `hne` and applies the lemma with `v := wraw`, `hv0 := hw0 ▸ Z.one_mem`. The four remaining clauses transfer through `(w : K⟦G⟧) = wraw`.
findings.benefit: It removes about 40 lines of Subtype/coercion plumbing that is currently written twice. The duplicate re-proof of the restriction's membership is also removed. The two public theorems would then show only their mathematical steps, and any change to the representation of the bounded integer part is made in one place.
